title_orig: Fortalitium fidei contra Judeos et Saracenos aliosque christiane fidei inimicos
title_es: Fortalitium de la fe contra judíos, sarracenos y otros enemigos de la fe cristiana (título español aproximado, traducción nuestra)
title_en: Fortress of the Faith against Jews and Saracens and other enemies of the Christian faith
edition_original: Antonius Koberger, Nuremberg, 1494 (copy read: Internet Archive item bub_gb_suVxAvfy1hoC, from a Google Books scan; PDF page 394 of 598 read as image). Other prints checked for the same passage: Fortalitium fidei 1487 (archive.org item FortalitiumFidei1487, djvu OCR only), Lyon 1511 (archive.org item FortalitiumFideiContraJudeos1511, djvu OCR only), jbc.bj.uj.edu.pl NDIGSTDR049423 (1494, djvu OCR only).
digital_url: https://archive.org/download/bub_gb_suVxAvfy1hoC/bub_gb_suVxAvfy1hoC.pdf#page=394 (PDF page 394 read as image; item page https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_suVxAvfy1hoC)
licence: Archive.org metadata: licenseurl http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/ (Public Domain Mark 1.0); scan by Google.
authenticity_note: Genuine work of Alfonso de Espina (attribution uncontested in the printed editions). Book IV sources its Muhammad material partly from other works that Espina names; the 'Historia orientalis' he cites was NOT identified by us.
notes: The passage is in Liber quartus, Secunda consideratio ('de vita et moribus Machometi'), first 'punctus' ('vita machometi fuit bestialis et libidinosa'). The printed folio number is not legible on the PDF page; cite as Liber IV, Consideratio II, p. [folio not read], PDF 394. The 1494 print has an alternate ordering in other copies; locate by the heading 'De vita et moribus machometi'.

title_orig: El Obispo de Jaen sobre la Seta Mahometana (Historia e impugnacion de la secta de Mahoma; title given in the 16th c. copy)
title_es: El Obispo de Jaén sobre la secta mahometana
title_en: The Bishop of Jaén on the Muslim sect
date: Attributed to 1300 (Pascual's last work, per Armengol 1908; the 16th-century codex title says MCCC but is not by the author); scholarly dating: 2nd half of 14th c. (González Muñoz, search snippet only); earliest surviving copy: Escorial, Ms. h-II-25, 16th c. (copy by Licenciado Núñez, per Armengol)
language: Castilian (Spanish), with Latin version printed beside it
genre: Polemical treatise (impugnación) with a life of Muhammad (ch. II on his wives)
edition_original: Fr. Pedro Armengol Valenzuela (ed.), 'Obras de S. Pedro Pascual ... en su lengua original, con la traduccion latina ... Volumen cuarto. El Obispo de Jaen sobre la Seta Mahometana', Roma: Imprenta Salustiana, 1908. Pages read: PDF pp. 84-85 (printed pp. 30-31) of archive.org item obrasdespedropascualmar4 (OCR and page image).
licence: archive.org metadata: https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/ (Public Domain Mark 1.0); the 1908 publication is also public domain by date.
authenticity_note: Attribution to Pascual is traditional and disputed; Armengol (1908) accepts it; González Muñoz (search snippet) calls it pseudo-Pascual. The Latin text printed beside the Spanish is a later translation (Armengol says it was made in the 17th c. for the canonisation process); it is NOT medieval. The Spanish text is the oldest form we can read.
notes: Armengol's footnote 2 on p. 30 reads 'Aicha, o Aiecha' (editor's note, 1908), i.e., he equates Axa with Aisha. Armengol's note 1 on Khadija. The Spanish 'Axa' appears throughout the chapter and on PDF pp. 84-125. The Spanish of chapter II is the passage to cite; the Latin is a late translation.

title_orig: Libro nueuamente imprimido que se llama confusion dela secta mahomatica y d'l Alcoran
title_es: Libro recién impreso llamado Confusión de la secta mahomética y del Alcorán
title_en: Newly printed book called Confusion of the Muhammadan sect and the Qur'an
genre: Polemical treatise (Spanish, from a Muslim convert)
edition_original: Valencia: Joan Joffre, 1515. Library of Congress, Lessing J. Rosenwald Collection, item 2021rosen1275 (page images and ALTO OCR read: LOC image 0060 and 0182, plus 0104-0107 for wife-number context).
licence: LOC Rosenwald collection: LOC item record lists no restriction in the fields we read (not checked further).
authenticity_note: The author is a former Muslim convert; the text is a Spanish polemic, not a neutral source. The page 182 aside is an addendum ('que me olvidé de ponerlo en el capítulo de las mugeres').
notes: The LOC record gives language 'english' (catalogue error); the text is Spanish.

title_orig: Contra principales errores perfidi Machometi et Turcorum sive Saracenorum (Ioannis de Turrecremata)
title_es: Contra los principales errores del pérfido Mahoma y de los turcos o sarracenos
title_en: Against the principal errors of the perfidious Muhammad and of the Turks or Saracens
date: c. 1459 (per a secondary citation in a search snippet; not verified)
edition_original: Rome, 1606 (Internet Archive item bub_gb_atVAUPHz_bYC, Google Books scan; djvu OCR read, no page image checked)
digital_url: https://archive.org/details/bub_gb_atVAUPHz_bYC (djvu OCR read; the PDF was not downloaded)
licence: archive.org metadata not checked for licence; the 1606 print is public domain by date.
authenticity_note: Attribution to Turrecremata is uncontested for the printed title; the 1606 print is later than the original.
notes: Searched the OCR for uxor/uxores, Aisa/Aixa/Aysa/Ayxa/Hayssa, Abubacer/Abubeq, matrimon, coniug, nupti, concubin: no Aisha named in the text read. Only the wife-count and lust passages found.
